issues.legal_issue: Wilful breach of an assurance given by counsel on a client’s behalf to a court constitutes civil contempt under Section 2(b) of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971.

Whether an assurance or undertaking is given to the court or to the opposing party depends on the circumstances and language used; breach of an undertaking given to the court attracts contempt jurisdiction.

A court exercising contempt jurisdiction may declare transactions made in wilful breach of its order or undertaking void and direct their reversal to prevent the contemnor or persons claiming under the contemnor from benefiting.
Beneficiaries of transactions made in contempt have no right to be impleaded or heard in contempt proceedings merely because they claim to be bona fide purchasers for value without notice.
An apology for contempt need not be accepted where the conduct is serious and the apology is not genuine contrition, even if it is unconditional or made at an early stage.
